title: JustinGuitar Lesson 2: Practice Routine (Chords, Anchor Finger, and Song Practice)
summary: In JustinGuitar’s Lesson 2: Practice Routine, Justin walks through a structured 20-minute beginner-friendly practice sequence designed to build chord accuracy, finger independence, and timing. The plan emphasizes four practice sessions per week, cautions about finger pain and overdoing it, and then steps through a chord-focused drill (E, A, and D chords) before a dedicated anchor-finger exercise that cycles through chord shapes. The routine includes short, timed drills on each chord, a pattern-based transition exercise, and a riff-focused segment (Peter Gunn theme) to develop picking and finger agility. A 10-minute song practice follows, prioritizing songs the student enjoys (notably Three Little Birds) and, for now, avoiding capo; tempo and rhythm targets are discussed, including keeping a steady rhythm with foot tapping and aiming for roughly 30 chord changes per minute in early stages. The module ends with guidance on when to progress, the importance of memorizing chords before moving on, and pointers to practice-along resources and the website for further materials and updates.
topics: Four-session weekly practice schedule (Mon-Tue-Wed off; Thu-Fri practice; weekend off)
E major chord two-minute drill (dead-note check, single-note pickup, final strum)
A major chord one-minute drill (chord accuracy and transition check)
D major chord one-minute drill (chord accuracy and transition check)
Anchor finger exercise (two minutes) with six-chord cycle: E-A-E-D-A-D
Transitional pattern practice: E to A, E to D, A to D, D to E, etc.
Three one-minute chord-change sessions: A-D, A-E, D-E
Memorization of new chords (E, A, D) before moving on
Riff practice: Peter Gunn theme with a backing track
Left-handed practice notes and managing tension
Ten-minute song practice: Three Little Birds and other song options
Capo guidance: avoid capo in Lesson 2; capo discussion in next lesson
Practice-along resources (website and app) and backing tracks
Tempo and rhythm targets: aiming for ~30 changes per minute among core chords
Foot-tap rhythm training to reinforce timing
Guidance on readiness to move to the next lesson
